overall_reason: A deploy list dressed in a purple-to-pink-to-orange gradient, with purple text throughout; the look comes from the AI default, not from the task.

score.reason: T-DEFAULT-AGENT and T-MIRROR fail: the gradient frame, gradient heading text and gradient button are the stock AI look, and T-SIGNATURE fails because state is no longer readable.

findings.where: frame, heading and Deploy button, 1440 and 375
findings.evidence: The frame uses linear-gradient(135deg, #7c3aed, #db2777, orange); the 'Recent deploys' heading and the 'Deploy' button use a #7c3aed to #db2777 gradient.
findings.before: Violet-pink gradient frame, gradient text and gradient button
findings.after: A neutral ground; one solid colour for the action
findings.why: The violet gradient is the most common generated-UI look and says nothing about deploys.

findings.evidence: All three status icons are the same violet outline, and names (#4c1d95) and timestamps (#a78bfa) are tinted violet: live, building and failed look alike.
findings.after: Colour reserved for deploy state (live, building, failed)
findings.why: The failed 'Pricing copy' deploy, the one row that needs action, does not stand out.

findings.evidence: The card itself uses a #faf5ff to #fdf2f8 gradient with a violet ring, so even the content layer carries the theme.
findings.after: Plain card ground; let the content carry the screen
findings.why: When every layer is themed, the theme is the content and the task recedes.

strengths: The underlying list structure (name, branch and author, time, one action) is sound and worth keeping.
not_investigated: 00-contract.md is absent: no brand authority, audience or overrides were available, so the item was read as an Operate composition (CON-018).
T-RIVAL-NAME cap: the composition names no client, so every placeholder label holds under any rival; the cap at 5 was not applied and the test was used only to spot default copy.
T-IDEA-CARRIES: single composition, there is no second screen to carry the idea.
T-DELETE-PICTURE and T-PROMISE-PICTURED: no lead image and no marketing promise, except where a finding says so.
T-COVER-TEXT: no brand theme or motif to recognise.
The caption above some frames ('Considered composition' / 'Composition problem') is fixture text from the capture host and was not judged.
